Players now have faces. Every list on the **Players** tab (online, whitelist, operators and bans) shows each player's head, with the hat layer, next to their name. Flytower fetches skins from Mojang itself and keeps them on disk under `/var/lib/flytower/skins`, so your browser never tells a third-party avatar site who plays on your server, a player's skin is checked again only once a day, and heads keep showing when Mojang is down. Offline-mode and unknown players get the default Steve or Alex head without anything being sent to Mojang.

Client-only mods can now be installed. Modrinth lets authors mark a project as running only on players' computers, and Flytower used to refuse those outright, even when a server mod needed one. Now a client-only project you list in the YAML, or add from **Add content** with the new **Show client-only** switch, is installed like anything else, and so is a client-only required dependency. The plan shows a warning naming it (and, for a dependency, the mod that needs it), so you know where to look if the server won't start. Search still hides client-only projects by default. See [Client-only mods](https://github.com/MattA-Official/mc-panel/blob/v1.2.0-beta.1/docs/content.md#client-only-mods).

Testing notes are in the "Player heads" and "Client-only mods" sections of [testing-1.2.0.md](https://github.com/MattA-Official/mc-panel/blob/v1.2.0-beta.1/docs/testing-1.2.0.md).
